```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5)
source("stock_functions.R")
source("display_utils.R")
```

# Portfolio

The stock symbols are read from `portfolio.txt` (one symbol per line).

```{r portfolio}
symbols <- read_portfolio("portfolio.txt")
symbols
```

# Importing the Stock Data

`load_stock_data()` downloads one year of daily prices from Yahoo Finance
with `quantmod::getSymbols()` and stores each stock as its own data frame.

```{r load}
stocks <- load_stock_data("portfolio.txt",
                          from = Sys.Date() - 365, to = Sys.Date())
sapply(stocks, nrow)
```

## Preview of the data

```{r preview, results='asis'}
for (sym in names(stocks)) {
  print(knitr::kable(tail(stocks[[sym]], 5), digits = 2,
                     caption = paste(sym, "- last 5 trading days")))
  cat("\n")
}
```

## Quote summary (Yahoo Finance style)

```{r quotes}
for (sym in names(stocks)) display_quote_summary(stocks[[sym]], sym)
```

# Basic Statistics

Statistics are calculated on the daily **Close** price: mean, median,
mode (prices rounded to whole dollars), standard deviation and the
20-day simple moving average (SMA).

```{r stats}
stats <- calculate_all_statistics(stocks, column = "Close", ma_window = 20)
display_statistics(stats$table)
```

# Visualizations

## Closing price with 20-day moving average

```{r ma-plots}
for (sym in names(stocks)) {
  plot_price_with_ma(stats$by_stock[[sym]], sym, 20)
}
```

## Candlestick charts (last 90 days)

```{r candles}
for (sym in names(stocks)) {
  plot_candlestick(stocks[[sym]], sym, 20)
}
```

## Comparing the portfolio

```{r compare}
plot_normalized_comparison(stocks)
plot_statistics_bar(stats$table)
```

# Notes

* The mode is not very meaningful for continuous price data, so the prices
  were rounded to whole dollars before finding the most frequent value.
* RY.TO and SHOP.TO are listed on the TSX, so their prices are in CAD while
  the other stocks are in USD.
* This is stage 1 of 3; the saved data will be reused for the technical
  indicators in the next assignment.
